newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican in near-total opposition to death penalty.
newsitem.headline: Vatican in near-total opposition to death penalty.

text.p: The next edition of the Roman Catholic Church's catechism will reflect Pope John Paul's near-total opposition to capital punishment, a senior Vatican cardinal said on Tuesday.

The catechism, a code of Catholic belief which was last updated in 1992, would state that cases in which capital punishment was acceptable had become extremely rare, Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger told a news conference.

Throughout history, the Church has held that the death penalty was sometimes permissible, particularly in times of war or widespread civil disorder, as a means of legitimate defence for the common good of society.
In his 1995 encyclical "The Gospel of Life", the Pope said advances in modern society's penal system had made such cases "practically non-existent".
Ratzinger, head of the Catholic Church's doctrinal office, said the next edition of the catechism, due out later this year, would take the encylical into account.
This would bring the Church the closest it has ever come to calling for a total ban on capital punishment.
The 76-year-old Pope has made several interventions in the past few months to appeal for clemency for inmates on death row in prisons in the United States.
Opponents of capital punishment have long urged the Pope to support a total ban.
